Layer 2 · Access

Twelve sectors, and what gates each one

The negative list decides whether you may own the business. The licence decides whether you may operate it. Both are checked here, sector by sector, because a founder who reads only the list usually stops one gate too early.

How to read this page

The access tag is about ownership: open, open with a licence, restricted, or closed. The gate line is about permission: the licence, the premises or the partner that a new company cannot get around. If either fails, the sector fails for you — regardless of how good the market looks.

Sector by sector

The detail behind each tag

Equity limits, the licence that matters, how long it takes, and what foreign founders usually discover too late.

咨询与专业服务

Consulting & professional services

The default WFOE: an invoice, a payroll and a desk.

Open
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned
The gate
Business licence only
Typical timeline
3–6 weeks

A WFOE can be registered for management consulting, marketing, technical advisory, market research and similar scopes. No sector licence is required for the company itself.

Registration is the easy part. The scope on the licence must match what you actually bill, and the line between consulting and regulated advice — legal, tax, securities, education, medical — is enforced when a client complains or an invoice looks wrong.

Watch for: Do not write 'investment advice', 'legal services' or 'medical consulting' into the scope because it sounds impressive. It invites a licence you do not have.

Read the sector guide

软件与SaaS

Software & SaaS

Sell code freely; sell access to a Chinese website and the telecom rules arrive.

Open, with a licence
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned
The gate
ICP filing; ICP/EDI licence for online services
Typical timeline
4–10 weeks

Software development and B2B licensing are open. Operating a commercial website or app that serves users in China generally needs an ICP filing, and paid online services may need an ICP or EDI licence — where foreign equity is capped.

The foreign-equity cap on value-added telecom services is the reason many software founders sell to businesses through a WFOE and keep the consumer platform offshore — or license it to a domestic partner.

Watch for: A server in Singapore does not remove the obligation if your customers, payment and marketing are in China. Ask a telecom lawyer before you build the billing flow.

Read the sector guide

电子商务与零售

E-commerce & retail

Selling into China and selling inside China are two different businesses.

Open, with a licence
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned
The gate
ICP/EDI, product registrations, food or cosmetics licences
Typical timeline
4–12 weeks

Cross-border e-commerce into China can be run from abroad through a bonded platform. Selling domestically — a Tmall or Douyin store operated by a Chinese entity — needs a local company, ICP filing and the product-specific registrations.

The margin is in the licence and the logistics, not the storefront. Food, cosmetics, supplements and medical devices each carry their own registration or filing, and a marketplace will ask for it before your first sale.

Watch for: Do not import inventory before the product registration is in the name of the entity that will sell it. Re-labelling a shipment is not a compliance strategy.

Read the sector guide

进出口与物流

Import/export & logistics

The simplest cash-flow business to start, and the hardest to get paid for.

Open, with a licence
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned
The gate
Customs registration; road transport licence for domestic trucking
Typical timeline
4–10 weeks

A trading WFOE can hold foreign-trade operator status and clear goods. International freight forwarding needs a filing; domestic road transport needs a road-transport licence and vehicles registered to the entity.

Import/export is a working-capital business. The entity is easy; the credit terms, the customs classification and the 90-day receivables are what decide whether it survives.

Watch for: A forwarder that offers to 'borrow' your import quota or invoice through a friend's company is offering you a tax problem with a Chinese name on it.

Read the sector guide

制造与硬件

Manufacturing & hardware

The negative list is no longer the obstacle; the landlord and the EIA are.

Open
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned
The gate
Environmental impact assessment, fire, safety, land use
Typical timeline
3–9 months

Foreign-investment restrictions in manufacturing were reduced to zero in the 2024 negative list. The gate is now environmental approval, factory zoning, fire and safety inspection — and the landlord's right to let you operate there.

A factory lease signed before the environmental impact assessment is a bet that the assessment will pass. In many districts it will not, and the deposit is gone. Budget for the EIA, utilities and a compliant waste contract before equipment.

Watch for: Do not accept a landlord's assurance that 'the address is fine for industry'. Ask for the zoning certificate and the previous tenant's EIA approval, in writing.

Read the sector guide

餐饮

Food & beverage

A restaurant is a property deal with a kitchen attached.

Open, with a licence
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned
The gate
Food business licence, fire, health, alcohol licence
Typical timeline
2–5 months

A restaurant WFOE needs a food business licence tied to the premises, a fire inspection, staff health certificates and — for alcohol — a separate liquor licence. The premises must be zoned for food service.

The address decides the business: grease traps, ventilation, gas, waste and neighbouring consent are all physical. A cheap unit that cannot pass the kitchen inspection is the most common way a foreign F&B founder loses a year.

Watch for: Do not sign a five-year lease on a site whose previous tenant was not a restaurant. The extraction and waste infrastructure is usually the whole problem.

Read the sector guide

教育与培训

Education & training

The widest gap between what founders plan and what is licensable.

Restricted
Foreign equity
Joint venture or domestic partner; compulsory education closed to FIEs
The gate
Private school licence; curriculum and teacher approvals
Typical timeline
6–18 months

Foreign-invested schools are limited to non-compulsory stages and generally require a Chinese partner. Compulsory education is closed to foreign ownership, and after-school tutoring in core subjects has been heavily restricted since 2021.

Language training, test prep, early-years and corporate training sit under different rules, and the local education bureau applies them differently. A licence to teach adults is not a licence to teach children.

Watch for: Do not open classrooms while the licence is 'in progress'. The inspection that closes you is usually triggered by a parent, not a competitor.

Read the sector guide

医疗与诊所

Healthcare & clinics

Pilot cities change; leases do not.

Restricted
Foreign equity
Generally joint venture; wholly foreign-owned pilot in selected cities
The gate
Medical institution licence; practitioner registration
Typical timeline
9–24 months

Medical institutions are generally limited to joint ventures, with a pilot allowing wholly foreign-owned hospitals in a changing list of cities and provinces. Every clinician needs a Chinese practising registration in the specialty.

The health commission, not the company registry, decides whether you can operate. Approval depends on beds, departments, equipment, infection control and the named medical director — and the process is local.

Watch for: Do not lease or equip a clinic until the local health commission confirms, in writing, that your proposed scope and ownership structure are eligible in that district.

Read the sector guide

旅游与酒店

Tourism & hospitality

Inbound is the niche a foreign founder can actually own.

Open, with a licence
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned for inbound; outbound travel closed to FIEs
The gate
Travel agency licence and deposit; hotel licences
Typical timeline
2–6 months

Inbound travel agencies can be wholly foreign-owned with a licence and a quality deposit. Outbound travel — selling trips that Chinese residents take abroad — is restricted to domestic-invested agencies. Hotels need fire, health and special-industry licences.

The licence and deposit are only the entry ticket. Distribution in China runs through platforms and licensed agencies, and a hotel's star rating is a licensing process, not a marketing label.

Watch for: If your product is 'we take Chinese guests abroad', you are in outbound travel. A WFOE cannot hold that licence, and routing it through a friend's agency is a compliance problem, not a structure.

媒体与内容

Media & content

The shortest part of the negative list to read, and the hardest to work around.

Closed or restricted
Foreign equity
News, publishing and film production prohibited; some content services via JV
The gate
Licences that are rarely granted to foreign-owned entities
Typical timeline
Not applicable for prohibited activities

News gathering, publishing, film production, distribution and cinema chains are prohibited to foreign investors. Advertising, design, events and some online content services are open, but the content itself is regulated.

Most foreign media founders end up as a production, advertising or technology company selling services to licensed Chinese publishers — not as the publisher. That is a different business with a different margin.

Watch for: Do not describe your entity as a 'media company' or 'publisher' in its scope unless you have the licence. The scope is evidence.

Read the sector guide

设计与创意

Design & creative

Design the brand freely; do not stamp the drawing.

Open, with qualifications for some work
Foreign equity
100% foreign-owned
The gate
Business licence; design qualifications for construction-related work
Typical timeline
3–8 weeks

Brand, industrial, interior and digital design are open. Construction design, engineering and anything that stamps a drawing for a permit require a Chinese design qualification and registered personnel, which a new WFOE will not have.

Creative founders underprice the qualification boundary. A studio that designs a fit-out is fine; a studio that signs the drawing for the fit-out permit is practising engineering without a licence.

Watch for: Keep the contract for construction documents with a qualified local design institute. Your name can be on the concept, not on the stamp.

金融与金融科技

Finance & fintech

A licensing business, not a software business.

Restricted
Foreign equity
Licence-specific caps; often joint venture or domestic control
The gate
Financial licence from the regulator before registration
Typical timeline
12–36 months, if at all

Payments, lending, securities, fund distribution, insurance and crypto-related activity each have their own regulator, capital requirement and foreign-equity cap. A software company that touches client money is regulated as a financial business.

The licence comes first, and it is usually granted to an entity with a domestic shareholder, a capital base and a regulatory history. A new WFOE with a good app is not a candidate for most financial licences.

Watch for: Do not hold, pool or transmit client funds through a consulting WFOE while 'waiting for the licence'. That is the fact pattern regulators treat as unlicensed payment business.

Read the sector guide

A sector is not a market. It is a licence, a premises standard, and a regulator who has seen your business model before.
